title: EvidenceAssessment/v1
description: A typed assessment of the evidence supporting a ScientificClaim, placing the claim on 11 ORTHOGONAL evidence axes. The axes are independent by construction: a movement on one axis never grants a movement on another. This is the load-bearing honesty property of the evidence model (see docs/contracts/evidence-model.md): READY is not COMPUTED (capability_state=ready does not imply the engine ran), COMPUTED is not VALIDATED (engine_execution=completed does not imply scientific_check=checked), a SAT/UNSAT-style answer yields at most scientific_check=checked (formal_check=proven REQUIRES a non-null formal_certificate_ref), formal proof is not empirical truth (formal_check never updates statistical_support or causal_identification), algorithmic cross-engine reproduction is not independent empirical replication (setting one never sets the other), and exportable evidence (integration_authority=proposal_only) is not admitted authority (admitted_a1_sandbox / admitted_a2 are reserved; SRL has no authority path). The assessment carries the two safety consts (canonical_writes=0, grants_authority=false). Canonical JSON contract: sorted keys, compact separators, UTF-8, no NaN/Infinity, trailing newline.

allOf.$comment: Probe is not compute: an import_probe exercise_level forbids engine_execution=completed in the same assessment. An import probe only checks the object imports / loads; it cannot have actually run the computation. This is encoded at schema AND python layer (orthogonality: probe_not_compute).
A failed engine run cannot have produced a checked scientific result: engine_execution=failed forbids scientific_check=checked (the engine did not complete, so no scientific output exists to check).

assessment_id.description: Content-addressed identity: sha256 over the canonical encoding of the assessment (without this field), prefixed 'sha256:'. Computed by srl.semantic.evidence.assessment_id. An assessment whose parents carry a prior assessment id forms a lineage chain (update_assessment threads the prior id).

subject_claim_id.description: The claim_id of the ScientificClaim/v1 this assessment evaluates. The assessment is about exactly one claim; the axes collectively describe the evidence standing behind that claim.

axes.description: The 11 ORTHOGONAL evidence axes. Each axis is an independent dimension of evidence; a movement on one axis never grants a movement on another (the orthogonality invariant enforced by srl.semantic.evidence).

capability_state.description: The claimed capability of the claim's backing software: unknown (not assessed), declared (the adapter/claim asserts it), profiled (an AdapterSemanticProfile admits it), ready (the operator asserts the capability is ready to run). ready is NOT compute — it only means the capability is asserted, not that the engine ran.

exercise_level.description: How far the claim's backing was actually exercised: none (not exercised), import_probe (it imports/loads but does not run), runtime_probe (it runs to a probe point), actual_compute (it ran the real computation). import_probe CANNOT yield engine_execution=completed (probe is not compute).

engine_execution.description: Whether the backing engine actually ran: not_run (never run), failed (ran and failed — no scientific output exists), completed (ran to completion). completed is NOT validated — it only means the engine finished, not that the scientific output was checked.

scientific_check.description: Whether the scientific output was independently checked against the claim: not_applicable (no scientific output to check), unchecked (output exists, not yet checked), checked (checked and consistent), contradicted (checked and the output contradicts the claim).

formal_check.description: The level of formal (machine-checkable) verification: not_applicable (no formal statement to check), unchecked (a formal statement exists, not yet checked), checked (a solver returned SAT/UNSAT or a checked certificate), proven (a verified, independently-checkable certificate exists — REQUIRES a non-null formal_certificate_ref). proven is NOT empirical truth; it only means the formal statement was discharged.

formal_scope.description: The scope of the formal statement relative to the claim: none (no formal statement), exact_statement (the formal statement is exactly the claim), restricted_model (the formal statement covers a restricted sub-model), full_model (the formal statement covers the full model). A proven statement over a restricted_model is honest about its scope.

statistical_support.description: The strength of statistical support for the claim: not_applicable, none, weak, moderate, strong. This axis is INDEPENDENT of the formal axes: a formal proof never updates statistical support (formal proof is not empirical truth).

causal_identification.description: The degree to which a causal effect is identified: not_applicable, assumed (a causal structure is assumed, not established), partially_identified, identified. This axis is INDEPENDENT of the formal axes: a formal proof never updates causal identification.

algorithmic_cross_engine_reproduction.description: Whether the computation reproduced across an independent engine: not_applicable, none, reproduced (a second engine agreed), divergent (a second engine disagreed). This axis is INDEPENDENT of independent_empirical_replication: algorithmic agreement is NOT independent empirical replication (setting one never sets the other).

independent_empirical_replication.description: Whether the empirical result was independently replicated: not_applicable, none, replicated (an independent empirical study confirmed it), contradicted (an independent study contradicted it). This axis is set ONLY by its own evidence_refs (with a distinct assessor); algorithmic reproduction never sets it.

integration_authority.description: The authority an assessment confers to integrate the claim into downstream artifacts: none (no integration authority), proposal_only (the claim may be cited as a proposal only), admitted_a1_sandbox (RESERVED — admitted to a sandbox integration tier; SRL has no authority path to set this), admitted_a2 (RESERVED — admitted to a full integration tier; SRL has no authority path to set this). In this codebase integration_authority defaults to none and can only be raised to proposal_only; admitted_* is rejected by the python builder.

evidence_refs.description: The object_ids of the evidence objects backing the axis movements (engine receipts, validation receipts, run receipts, formal certificates, independent studies). Each axis movement SHOULD be backed by an evidence_ref; an update_assessment call carries the evidence_ref that justifies the delta.

assessor.description: Who produced the assessment: adapter (the backend adapter self-assessed), validator (an independent validator assessed), operator (the operator asserted), bridge (a cross-system bridge assessed). Distinct assessors back distinct axes (e.g. algorithmic reproduction vs independent empirical replication are set only by their own evidence with a distinct assessor).

created_utc.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp at seconds precision (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). No offset, no fractional seconds.

parents.description: The assessment_ids of prior assessments in the lineage chain. update_assessment threads the prior assessment id here so the full prior state is carried. An assessment with empty parents is a root assessment (the first assessment of a claim).

canonical_writes.description: Safety const: an assessment is immutable once authored. Always 0; a non-zero value is a contract violation.

grants_authority.description: Safety const: an assessment never grants authority on its own. Always false; a true value is a contract violation. integration_authority=proposal_only is an admission, not an authorization.
